route: Residence route not confirmed from an official page: the Belgian Immigration Office site (dofi.ibz.be) sits behind a human-check and I could not read it, and the search budget ran out before I could find another official visa page. A search result suggested a long-stay D visa requires proof of cover for Belgium and sufficient means, with private insurance accepted at the visa stage. Treated as unverified.
policy: Once registered in the National Register (resident), the person must join a mutualite and pay the INAMI/RIZIV 'cotisation personnelle' because no social contribution is paid on professional income: 931.12 EUR per quarter per person from 1 January 2026 (normal rate). Reduced rates exist for lower incomes. Mutualite membership fees and supplementary (hospitalisation) insurance are extra and were not priced.
working: 931.12 EUR per quarter / 3 = 310.37 EUR per month per person. Couple: 2 x 310.37 = 620.75 EUR per month (620.7467). If both qualify for the 'revenu < ceiling' rate (465.55 per quarter): 2 x 465.55 / 3 = 310.37 EUR per month.

eu_citizen_difference: An EU citizen with a right of residence is registered and pays the same contribution once a resident; EU citizens may also arrive with EHIC/S1 cover. A non-EU newcomer relies on private cover for the visa and then the mutualite.
spot_check: No independent figure. The previous year's contribution (2025) was 912.91 EUR per quarter on the same INAMI page, so 931.12 is a 2% indexation.
uncertainty: Unverified: whether a non-EU newcomer registered on a first permit can join immediately or serves a waiting period (a 2010 guide and a Fedasil sheet mention six months, unclear scope). Unverified: whether a spouse can be a dependant (personne a charge) on the other's contribution, which would halve the figure. The mutualite's own fee, the mandatory hospital top-up and the visa-stage private policy cost were not found. The visa rule is unsourced.

statutory_must_pay.what: INAMI/RIZIV personal contribution, 2 x 931.12 EUR a quarter, as in the first round (2 x 310.375 a month).

private_plan.terms: In-patient only: single-room supplements up to 100 EUR a day, doctors' fee supplements at twice the legal tariff, care 30 days before and 90 days after hospital stay; maximum 100 EUR a year excess in a single room. No out-patient cover beyond that. 6-month waiting period. Needs MC membership (the INAMI contribution covers it).
private_plan.pricing: Brochure 2026 gives 31.97 EUR a month per adult aged 25-49, for people who subscribe before age 45; a surcharge applies for subscribing after 45 and the brochure does not give its size, so 2 x 31.97 = 63.94 is a lower bound for a 45-year-old couple. Market guides quote 60-90 EUR a month per person for single-room cover (secondary, comparator site).
